verdict.rationale: AMD ships an official ROCm Core SDK with HIP and roc* libraries, a profiler SDK and a debug agent. Its docs list the RX 9070 XT (gfx1201) in the official PyTorch and JAX install guides, and ROCm 7.2.1 is stated to support Radeon 9000 Series, so developers can build against first-party SDKs for this card. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of SDK use on the 9070 XT; Windows support is documented only for PyTorch (Linux covers PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, ONNX); and the individual math libraries do not explicitly confirm RDNA4 support.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: You can build the ROCm Core SDK from source using the open-source unified build system TheRock.
ROCm™ 7.2.1 supports the latest Radeon™ 9000 Series (RDNA™ 4) and select 7000 Series (RDNA™ 3) GPUs
Libraries prefixed with `hip*` are portable wrappers that implement NVIDIA CUDA-equivalent APIs, allowing CUDA applications to be ported to AMD GPUs with minimal code changes.
It uses rocRAND in a ROCm environment and provides C, C++, and Python API wrappers.
